title: 4 days Upper Lower + 1 Arm day Program review
summary: NH reviews a viewer's five-day upper/lower plus arm day program, praising its lift rotations within the range of specificity and its evolving rep ranges. He recommends trimming isolation volume, avoiding repeated sets of three on bench, not pairing SSB squats with good mornings, and adding a quad-focused squat variation on the second lower day.
claims: Rotate lift variations within days to create a two-week A/B rotation without a separate week A and week B; the day's skeleton and muscle groups stay the same
4-8 reps for 3 sets is an excellent evolving rep range for bench press
Repeating sets of three up to eight sets on bench isn't conducive to progression; it forces you to sandbag rather than produce quality heavy reps
NH prefers three strength sets followed by two paused back-off sets on the main press
Vertical pulls are mandatory on an upper day; if you can't weight them yet, don't
The limiting factor on pull-ups isn't the upper back, which handles huge volume and recovers fast, but connective tissue of elbows, shoulders and biceps tendon
Using the same pull-up grip every time leads to injury over time; vary grips, and a multi-grip bar is a good home gym investment
NH does pull-ups every day and assigns a specific grip to each day
Overhead pressing 5x8-12 is a lot of volume but presses tolerate high volume well
Variations close in specificity (e.g. barbell to axle overhead press) feed the main lift; seated or kneeling is further away, and lateral raises carry almost nothing over
If weighted chins were done wide, row to the sternum or higher to hit traps and upper back; after close-grip chins a normal Pendlay row is fine
5x8-15 is too much for skull crushers; 4x8-12 is better to keep intensity up while protecting the elbows
Small muscle groups respond to intensity just as well as large ones; doing 5 sets of 10-15 for arms is junk volume
A strong pump can limit performance because the gorged muscle stiffens before it is actually fatigued
Don't superset strength work such as the main bench press or weighted chins
A 20 lb jump on squats once 3x10 is reached is a lot; waiting for all sets to hit 10 before adding weight is sandbagging
The SSB squat is the opposite of a front squat: it folds you over and taxes the posterior chain more
Don't pair good mornings with back squats or other posterior-chain-heavy squats on the same day; front squats pair well with them
Good mornings don't forgive fatigue; NH treats them as the main hip hinge of the day, like a heavy deadlift, even in high reps
For good mornings 3x10-15 is excellent; never go below about 6 reps with 2 in reserve (around an 8RM) for hypertrophy
When two calf raise variations compete in a session, the one done first progresses the most
Superset reverse curls (elbow flexion with crushing grip) with wrist curls; they complement each other for the forearms
NH usually prescribes 10-15 reps for shrugs
Lower body days end up with upper back work like pull-ups added because they are short, so they aren't truly lower days
Calves are small and burn out quickly in a session but respond well to volume and frequency, so training them on rest days is fine
Pressing overhead twice a week is necessary if you want big shoulders
5 sets of 6-12 is a good evolving rep range: a true 12 on set one drops to about 6-7 by set five
Cable rows are one of NH's favourite cable movements for the upper back
Keep bodyweight chin-ups even when doing weighted ones; never turn your back on bodyweight work, it helps injury prevention
3-5 reps is NH's favourite deadlift range; sometimes one set of five is enough; he doesn't chase tonnage on deadlifts
Snatch-grip and deficit deadlifts are very similar: both lower the hips and add knee flexion; deficit loads the lumbar more, snatch grip the upper back and quads
On the second lower day replace leg extensions with a quad-focused squat (Zercher or SSB front squat) for 3x6-10, complementing lumbar-focused deadlifts
Introduce movements with a learning curve extremely light and ramp up slowly
Heavy weighted stretches for traps (or rack pulls) are time-efficient if trap bar shrugs aren't working
EZ-bar curls for 3x5-8 are great; biceps respond very well to high intensity
Grippers are not great for forearm hypertrophy but build grip strength that helps you hold weights for forearm work
Neck, abs and calves can be trained as a circuit on rest days
exercises: main hip hinge; dangerous when fatigued
easy setup; floor pull adds fatigue
more knee flexion and range of motion
